festivals.title: Nepali New Year
festivals.description: The first day of the Nepali calendar, marking the start of the new Bikram Sambat year. Celebrated with fairs, family gatherings, and cultural programs across the country.

festivals.title: Nepali Loshar
festivals.description: New year celebration observed by several Himalayan and hill communities, marked with traditional food, music, and dance.

festivals.title: Sithi Nakha
festivals.description: A traditional Newar festival dedicated to cleaning water sources and wells, and worshipping Kumar, the god of water and prosperity.

festivals.title: Ghantakarna
festivals.description: A festival commemorating the destruction of the demon Ghantakarna, observed with effigy burning to ward off evil spirits.

festivals.title: Gunla Begins
festivals.description: The start of the sacred Newar Buddhist month of Gunla, marked by daily temple visits, fasting, and traditional music processions.

festivals.title: Naag Panchami
festivals.description: A day dedicated to worshipping serpent deities (Naags) for protection from snakebites and to bring good fortune and rain.

festivals.title: जनै पूर्णिमा / रक्षा बन्धन / पूर्णिमा व्रत / ऋषितर्पणी / क्वाति खाने दिन / संस्कृत दिवस
festivals.description: A sacred day when Hindu men change their janai (sacred thread) and people tie a raksha bandhan thread on their wrist for protection and good health.

festivals.title: गाईजात्रा (काठमाडौं उपत्यका बिदा) / विश्व आणविक परिक्षण विरुद्धको दिवस
festivals.description: A day dedicated to worshipping serpent deities (Naags) for protection from snakebites and to bring good fortune and rain.

festivals.title: श्रीकृष्ण जन्माष्टमी / गाैरा पर्व / गोरखकाली पूजा / दुर्वाष्टमी
festivals.description: Celebration of the birth of Lord Krishna, observed with fasting, devotional singing, and midnight prayers at temples.

festivals.title: हरितालिका तीज (महिला कर्मचारीहरूलाई मात्र) / गणेश चतुर्थी व्रत / राष्ट्रिय धर्मसभा दिवस / राष्ट्रिय बाल दिवस
festivals.description: A festival celebrated by women with fasting, singing, and dancing, praying for marital happiness and the wellbeing of their husbands and family.

festivals.title: Indra Jatra Begins
festivals.description: An eight-day street festival in Kathmandu honoring Indra, the god of rain, featuring masked dances and the Living Goddess Kumari's chariot procession.

festivals.title: Ghatasthapana
festivals.description: The first day of the Dashain festival, marking the ceremonial planting of barley seeds that will be used as blessings on Vijaya Dashami.

festivals.title: Vijaya Dashami
festivals.description: The most important day of Dashain, when elders bless younger family members with tika and jamara, symbolizing victory of good over evil.

festivals.title: Laxmi Puja (Tihar)
festivals.description: A day of the Tihar festival dedicated to worshipping Goddess Laxmi for wealth and prosperity, homes are lit with oil lamps and decorated with rangoli.

festivals.title: Bhai Tika
festivals.description: The final day of Tihar celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters, with sisters applying tika and offering blessings for their brothers' long life.

festivals.title: Yomari Punhi
festivals.description: A Newar harvest festival celebrated by making yomari, a steamed rice-flour delicacy filled with molasses or sesame, to give thanks for the harvest.

festivals.title: Udhauli Parba
festivals.description: A harvest festival celebrated primarily by the Kirat community, marking the descent of birds and people from the hills, with traditional Sakela dance.

festivals.title: Maghe Sankranti
festivals.description: A festival marking the transition of the sun into the Capricorn zodiac and the beginning of longer days, celebrated with foods like sesame sweets and sweet potatoes.

festivals.title: Sonam Losar
festivals.description: New year festival celebrated by Tamang and other Himalayan communities, observed with family gatherings, traditional dances, and feasts.

festivals.title: Maha Shivaratri
festivals.description: A major festival honoring Lord Shiva, marked with all-night vigils, fasting, and large gatherings of devotees at Pashupatinath Temple.

festivals.title: Gyalpo Losar
festivals.description: The Tibetan new year celebrated by Sherpa and other Himalayan communities with prayers, dances, and festive family meals.

festivals.title: Holi (Fagu Purnima)
festivals.description: The festival of colors celebrated with the throwing of colored powder and water, symbolizing the arrival of spring and victory of good over evil.

festivals.title: Ram Nawami
festivals.description: A festival celebrating the birth of Lord Rama, observed with recitations of the Ramayana, devotional singing, and temple visits.

festivals.title: Chaite Dashain
festivals.description: A smaller-scale version of Dashain celebrated in the month of Chaitra, marked by worship of Goddess Durga.
